nora (AE): FYI LargeCorp wants an on‑prem pilot in their isolated COLO. Key asks: 1) how do we package/transport bundles for a locked jumpbox, 2) delta/patch cadence, 3) pilot pricing that covers secure delivery. They also pushed a security questionnaire.

liam (SE): Quick answers: packaging can be a signed tarball or an OCI image depending on their intake process. For strictly offline ingestion we support USB delivery + signed metadata. We have a chunked delta format to reduce transfer.

anjali (Security): They asked about verification and audit trail. We require signed bundles (RSA-4096) and an SBOM. We'll provide verification instructions and a signed attest file containing release hash + build metadata.

liam (SE): Example minimal verification snippet to give them: 
```
# verify signature on jumpbox
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify redwood-release.pub -signature redwood-bundle-v2.sig redwood-bundle-v2.tar.gz
# sanity check bundle contents
sha256sum redwood-bundle-v2.tar.gz
```

pete (Infra Ops): Operational constraints: jumpbox must be a hardened host (we recommend RHEL8.6+) with disk >= 20GB for unpack, and at least 8GB RAM to run the runtime validation. If they insist on Windows jumpbox we can still support but need different unpack scripts.

nora (AE): They want to avoid frequent ops work. What's realistic for cert rotation and upgrades?

anjali (Security): For air-gapped: certificate rotation and bundle signing key custody are manual. We propose two options in SOW: 
- Option A: Quarterly certificate rotation + signed bundles delivered for each release.
- Option B: 6-month rotation if customer stores jumpbox private key behind an HSM/KMS and we get attestation.
We can't accept 12-month rotation without compensating controls.

ira (Legal): For pilot SOW: we typically include a limited SLA (best-effort support with defined escalation) and an indemnity carveout for offline installs. Commercial will sign a short SOW with packaging fee + monthly reserved pilot capacity.

liam (SE): Patch cadence recommendation:
- Pilot: monthly maintenance (security + small bugfixes) + 1 mid-pilot minor version upgrade.
- Emergency patches: signed hotfix bundles delivered via same channel.
Delta sizes: full trimmed bundle ~900MB (runtime + small model), delta patches ~120-350MB depending on model layers changed.

nora (AE): Ballpark cost for customer to budget?

pete (Infra Ops): Typical: $12k one-time packaging & secure-delivery + $8k/month reserved pilot node capacity (includes 24/7 ingest support during delivery windows). Can adjust if they need additional on-site help.

nora (AE): They also asked for a checklist to complete their security questionnaire quickly. Can we assemble short answers?

anjali (Security): I'll produce template answers for the questionnaire covering: signing algorithm, SBOM availability, verification steps, supported OS, minimum kernel, FIPS mode support, KMS/HSM options, audit logs retention (we recommend 90 days for pilot), and contact for emergent CVEs.

liam (SE): I'll draft a short runbook with these items and include sample commands and the expected output format (checksums, service-up checks). Example health probe: `curl --unix-socket /var/run/redwood.sock http://localhost/ready` returns JSON with pid + uptime.

deploy-bot: release-packager: generated redwood-bundle-v2.tar.gz and redwood-bundle-v2.sig (sha256: a1b2c3f4...).

ira (Legal): For SOW language, include: acceptance criteria (successful run of validation runbook), delivery method (USB or secured jumpbox pull), cert rotation option chosen, and pricing table. We'll exclude SLA credits for pilot installs.

nora (AE): Action items: Liam + Anjali to post runbook + questionnaire answers by EOD tomorrow. Pete to confirm packaging fee range and any on-call uplift. Ira to draft a 1‑page SOW snippet. I'll book a follow-up with LargeCorp for Friday. :thumbsup:

liam (SE): On it.

anjali (Security): Drafting now.

pete (Infra Ops): Confirming packaging uplift, will post numbers shortly.

nora (AE): Thanks team.
